title: Packet loss: TCP retransmissions
summary: 9 TCP segments were sent again on 4 connection(s); the worst sender retransmitted 3.7% of its data. Retransmission means a segment (or its ACK) was lost or badly delayed, which costs throughput and adds delay. 42 duplicate ACKs and 0 fast retransmissions confirm the receiver noticed gaps. 1 were spurious (data already acknowledged), pointing at delayed ACKs or an aggressive retransmission timer rather than real loss. Most retransmissions were sent *towards* the capture side, so packets were lost before they reached the capture point.
